title: World War I
note: Rival alliances, an arms race, imperial competition and nationalism turned a Balkan assassination in June 1914 into a world war. Trench stalemate made it a war of attrition and total war. The United States entered in 1917, Russia left after its revolution, and the 1919 Treaty of Versailles imposed harsh terms on Germany.

read.title: The war to end all wars
text: By 1914 Europe was split into two armed camps. Germany and Austria-Hungary were allied, while France, Russia and Britain had drawn together in the Triple Entente. Britain and Germany raced to build battleships, and every great power had war plans ready. On June 28, 1914, Gavrilo Princip, a member of the Black Hand, killed Archduke Franz Ferdinand in Sarajevo. Austria-Hungary, promised German support, declared war on Serbia. Within a week, Russia, Germany, France and Britain were at war.

Germany's plan was to defeat France quickly by marching through neutral Belgium, but the attack was stopped at the Marne. Both sides dug trenches from the North Sea to Switzerland. Machine guns, artillery and poison gas made attacks across no man's land deadly; at Verdun and the Somme in 1916, armies suffered hundreds of thousands of casualties for a few miles of ground. Governments rationed food, drafted millions and put factories to work for the war.

German submarine attacks and the Zimmermann Telegram brought the United States into the war in April 1917. Revolution took Russia out. Fresh American troops helped turn the tide, and the fighting stopped on November 11, 1918. The Treaty of Versailles blamed Germany for the war and demanded reparations, leaving bitterness that would help cause another war.
